newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian race row politician under investigation.
newsitem.headline: Australian race row politician under investigation.

text.p: Controversial Australian race row politician Pauline Hanson was being investigated over allegations she had abused parliamentary benefits, a government official said on Wednesday.
Hanson, responsible for sparking a bitter racism debate, was under investigation for travel claims she made for six trips in the lead-up to the launch of her One Nation party on April 11.
A spokesman for Administrative Services Minister David Jull said it was believed the flights between Australian cities were unrelated to either parliamentary or electorate business.
"We wrote to her on April 23 because there were about six flights she made prior to the launch of her One Nation party which we were a bit concerned about," the spokesman said.
"We think they don't fall within her entitlements. We just have a feeling that her flights were basically probably used for publicity for the launch of her party."
Under the rules for entitlements for Australian politicians, taxpayers meet the cost of travel allowances and flights only if the trips taken are for parliamentary or electorate business.
The spokesman said Hanson had not responded to the letter and the minister would write to her again in the next week if there was still no response.

The Hanson investigation follows a series of travel allowance abuses by politicians. Independent senator Mal Colston was recently forced to repay nearly A$7,000 (US$5,400) for several irregularities in his travel claims.
In addition, one government politician and a former government senator have been charged with fraud relating to their travel allowances.
